Petitioners have filed the petition U/sec.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, claiming the compensation amount of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the respondents.

Priyanka Dwivedi vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87558288/
1 2.

Petitioners case is as Follows:
Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children and petitioner No.5 &
6 are the parents of the deceased Pushparaj Dwivedi.
That on 08.12.2024 at about 3.00 pm, Pushparaj Dwivedi was crossing the Bengaluru-Kolar road, near Kolathuru Gate, wherein the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg No.KA-40-F-1468, drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Pushparaj Dwivedi and caused the accident, in the accident Pushparaj Dwivedi sustained grievous injuries and he died due to the accidental injuries and was shifted to MVJ Hospital, wherein he died due to the accidental injuries.
Autopsy was conducted at Govt Hospital, Hosakote.
Petitioners have performed the funeral and obsequies as per their customs and they have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- for the same.

3. Petitioners alleged that Late.Pushparaj Dwivedi was aged about 44 yeas of age as on the date of the accident and prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy and he was working as JCB driver and was earning Rs.35,000/- per month., and he was the only earning member for their family.

They alleged accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle and the Jurisdictional police have registered the case against the driver of the aforesaid offending vehicle in Cr.No.361/2024.

Petitioners alleged that the respondent is the owner of the offending vehicle and he is the insurer for the offending vehicle accordingly they are liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and they prays this tribunal to award the compensation amount with interest by allowing the petition.
4.

After filing of the petition, notice served to the respondent, respondent appeared through their/its counsel and filed power and their written statement by denying the entire version of the petitioners in toto.
Respondent specifically denied the age, income and profession of the deceased and contended that the deceased had died due to his own negligent act and prays this Tribunal to dismiss the petition.

5. In order to prove the case, the Petitioner No.1 examined herself as PW-1 and examined the employer of the deceased as PW-2, produced and marked 17 documents which are at Ex.P1 to 17 and they are fully cross examined.
Respondent has not chosen to lead his evidence and there is no material on record to show that respondent is prevented from leading the evidence accordingly evidence of respondent is taken as Nil.
6. I have heard the arguments for the counsel appearing for both the sides and I have perused the entire records.

7. On the basis of pleadings, I have framed the following Issues:
Priyanka Dwivedi vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87558288/
2 ISSUES

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1.Whether the petitioners prove that on 08.12.2024 at about 3.00 pm, Pushparaj Dwivedi was crossing the Bengaluru-Kolar road, near Kolathuru Gate, wherein the driver of KSRTC Bus bearing Reg No.KA- 40-F-1468, drove it with high speed, rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Pushparaj Dwivedi and caused the accident, in the accident Pushparaj Dwivedi sustained grievous injuries and he died due to the accidental injuries as alleged in the petition.?

2 Whether respondent proves that the accident occurred due to the negligent act of the deceased as contended in the written statement.?
3. Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?
4.
What order
or award?

8. After carefully going through the evidence placed on record and taking into consideration of facts and attending circumstances of the case, my findings to the above issues are as follows;
 Issue no.1: In the Affirmative  Issue no.2: In the Negative  Issue no.3: In partly Affirmative,
 Issue No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 REASONS  9. Issues No.1 to 3 :- I have taken these issues together for common discussion, so as to avoid the repetition of facts and reasoning.
PW.1 being the petitioner no.1 and the wife of the deceased Pushparaj Dwivedi, she reiterated the petition averments in her examination-in-chief affidavit.
10. According to the petitioners, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In order to prove the actionable negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, Petitioners have tendered the FIR, complaint, police intimation, mahazar, sketch,
IMV report, Inquest, PM report and final report which are at Ex.P1 to 9.
11.
On perusal and analysis of the aforesaid documents it is evident that Late Pushparaj Dwivedi died due to the accidental injuries.

Ex.P.11 is the reply notice given by the respondent wherein they admit that Nagaraja Chari S/o Shiva Chari was the driver of the offending bus and he was having valid DL as on the date of the accident.
Ex.P.9 is the final report filed against the Nagaraja Chari after fair investigation and it is not disputed by the respondent.
The final report is the prime facie proof for the negligent act of the driver of the offending vehicle.

In the cross examination of PW-1 Priyanka Dwivedi vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87558288/
3 nothing has been elicited to disprove the petition allegations.
Respondent has not chosen to lead the evidence to probabilise his defence as contended in the written statement.
12. Further more, PW-2 deposed that deceased was operating the JCB in their company and he was drawing monthly salary of Rs.23,000/-.
Ex.P15 is the appointment letter of the deceased.
Ex.P.16 are the pay slips.
The aforesaid documents establishes that the deceased was working as JCB operator and he was drawing monthly salary Rs.23,010/-.
The aforesaid facts corroborates with oral testimony of PW-2.
Nothing worth is elicited from the mouth of PW-2 to disbelieve the facts.

Accordingly the monthly income of the deceased is assessed as Rs.23,010/-.
13.
Ex.P11 is the Adhaar card and Ex.P.13 is the DL of the deceased and as per the entry therein the date of birth of the deceased 30.09.1980.
Accordingly the age of the deceased as on the date of the accident was 45 years.
Accordingly the multiplier 14 is applicable.
14. Deceased was self employee and above 40 years and below 50 years of age, accordingly 25% of the future prospectus has to be added towards monthly salary.
Deceased has left behind 6 dependents accordingly 1/4 should be deducted from his monthly income towards his personal expenses.

15. The loss of dependency is calculated as follows:
1 Monthly income Rs.23,010/-
25% added towards future prospectus Rs.5,752/-
Rs. 28,762/-
2 Less; 1/4 for personal expenses Rs. 7,190/- 4

Monthly income Rs.21,572/-
Rs.21,572 (income)X 12 (month) X 14 Rs.36,24,096/- (Multiplier ) Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.36,24,096/- as compensation under the head Loss of Dependency.

16. Loss of estate;
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Pranaya sethi case, Tribunal has to award Rs.15,000/- as compensation under this head.

17 . Funeral Expenses, transportation etc., Accordingly as per the judgment in Praneya sethi case,
minimum amount of Rs.15,000/- can be awarded under this head.
18. Loss of Consortium :
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Magma GIC V/s Nanuram case, wherein the concept of consortium is categorically discussed.

In the present case petitioner no.1 is the Priyanka Dwivedi vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87558288/
4 wife, petitioner No.2 to 4 are the children and petitioner No.5 & 6 are the parents of the deceased and they are entitled for consortium of Rs.40,000/- each.
Accordingly petitioners are entitled for Rs.2,40,000/- as compensation under this head.
Except the aforesaid compensation amount, petitioners are not entitled for compensation in any other heads.

19. In total the petitioners are entitled for compensation as follows;
Sl No. Compensation under the Head Amount 1 Loss of dependency Rs.36,24,096/-
2 Loss of estate Rs. 15,000/-
3 Funeral expenses & transportation Rs. 15,000/- 4 Loss of Consortium Rs. 2,40,000/-
[S In total petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.38,94,096/-.
20. Rate of Interest:

The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, in Sarala Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121, wherein it is held that it is just and proper to award interest at the rate of 6% p.a.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly I award the interest at the rate of 6% P.A on the compensation amount form the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
21. Liability:
As per the police records the accident took place due the sole rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle which belongs to Respondent.
It is not disputed that the respondent is the insurer of the said offending vehicle which caused the accident and the validity of the said policy is not disputed.
Accordingly respondent is liable and has to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner.
Accordingly respondent is directed to pay the compensation amount along interest before this tribunal with in one month from the date of the Judgment.
Accordingly I am answering issue no.1 in the affirmative, issue no.2 in the negative and issue no.3 in partly affirmative.
22. Issue No.4;

For the foregoing reason and discussion, on the aforesaid issues, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 is partly allowed with cost.
Petitioners are entitled for compensation amount of Rs.38,94,096/- with interest @
6% p.a. from the date of claim petition, till realization.
Priyanka Dwivedi vs K.S.R.T.C on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87558288/
5
The respondent is directed to deposit the entire compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within one month from the date of the judgment.
Petitioner No.1 to 6 are entitled for Rs.6,49,016/- each with interest.

After depositing the compensation amount with interest, petitioner No.1, 2, 5 & 6 is permitted to withdraw their entire share of compensation amount with interest there on by complying the mandate of circular No.39/2020 dt. 17.01.2020,

Further, the entire share of minor petitioner No.3 and 4 shall be deposited in their names in any nationalized bank till they attained the age of majority and petitioner No.1 shall be the nominee for the both.
Issue intimation to the banker not to allow the petitioner No.3 & 4 not to create encumbrance on the deposited amount and not to permit them for premature withdrawal of their deposit amount.
Advocate fee of Rs.1,000/- is fixed.
Any interim applications pending if any stands disposed of.
Draw award accordingly.
